Space Lattice Theory is a physical model proposed by the American engineer Bruce Nappi in which space is not an empty void but a densely packed, crystal-like lattice filling the universe, and in which everything we call matter consists of movable defects — dislocations — in that lattice .
Nappi presents it as a Grand Unification: a single physical medium from which matter, energy, time, cause and effect, gravity and the electromagnetic and nuclear forces are all derived, rather than a collection of separate fundamental entities and interactions. Its central appeal, in his account, is that the explanations it produces are simple and visualizable — the model borrows directly from the well-understood physics of defects in ordinary solids, where dislocations move, interact, attract and repel through an elastic medium.
The theory is set out in his 244-page monograph Space Lattice Theory (2015) and in the book Introduction to Space Lattice Theory: Elements for a Grand Unification of Physics .
The lattice
In place of empty space, Nappi proposes that the universe is packed with a single kind of small object, which he designates an "Aa" . These pack together into a lattice of face-centred cubic structure, infinite in extent and possessing the simplest possible elasticity — in effect a solid, massive crystalline ether .
Everything else follows from the mechanics of that solid. Matter is not a substance added to space but a topological defect in it; energy propagates as elastic disturbance; forces between particles are the stress fields by which defects in a crystal influence one another. Abstract
Space Lattice Theory is a study of the fundamental structure of the universe. The study asks what that structure might be like if, instead of being mostly an empty void, space is a densely packed, crystal-like Lattice, and the existence and interaction of what we call matter is due to movable defects or dislocations in the Lattice. This theoretical study found that a dislocation model could produce a comprehensive set of simple, visualizable explanations for most of the concepts of physics, including many that are currently unanswered. It explains matter, time, cause and effect, energy, and how energy converts to matter. It explains gravity and electric and magnetic fields; how they can be physical realities, and how they could work.
Space Lattice Theory supports a “big bang”-like beginning for a 3-D “visible” universe, explaining how it could easily emerge from what appears to be the nothingness of space, but without having to change any laws of physics. Puzzles like the particle-wave nature of photons are explained. Problems with current theories for subatomic particles, cosmology and Special Relativity are discussed. New models are suggested.
Most significantly, Space Lattice Theory presents a comprehensive model for the Grand Unification of all forces and matter in the universe.

Spacetime curvature is the proposal, central to general relativity , that gravitation is not a force acting between bodies but a property of the geometry through which they move. Mass and energy deform a four-dimensional continuum of space and time; bodies then follow the straightest available paths through that deformed geometry, and what Newton described as an attractive force appears as an artefact of the shape of the arena.
It is the single most disputed idea documented on this wiki. Roughly 184 pages engage with it directly — some 84 papers, 44 scientist biographies and 14 books — and around 450 discuss curvature in some form. That places it above push gravity , tired light and the Casimir effect in the volume of material collected here.
What the standard account claims
Albert Einstein 's field equations relate the curvature of spacetime at a point to the energy and momentum present there. The account is economical: one geometric statement replaces both the gravitational force and the flat background of special relativity, and it has passed every precision test put to it, from the perihelion advance of Mercury and the bending of starlight to the Shapiro delay, gravitational redshift, frame dragging, the orbital decay of binary pulsars and the direct detection of gravitational waves in 2015.
Its critics do not generally dispute those measurements. What they dispute is the interpretation — whether geometry is the cause of gravitation or merely an efficient bookkeeping for it.
The objection from mathematisation

Abstract
Six samples of objects have been analyzed in order to check whether the redshift asymmetry discovered by Rubin et al. is a general effect. The results for all samples are consistent with the existence of the asymmetry. Its average magnitude is = 1300 + 210 km/s. The asymmetry vanishes at large distances. Various interpretations of the effect have been discussed. Arguments are given in favour of a non-Doppler redshift occurring in the intergalactic space within the Local Supergalaxy and other concentrations of galaxies.

Overview
This is a short observational paper by Jean-Claude Pecker , Jean Pierre Vigier and Toivo Jaakkola , written in 1975 and published without revision in Apeiron fifteen years later. It asks whether the hemispheric redshift asymmetry that Rubin, Ford and Rubin reported in 1973 for Sc I galaxies is a general property of the sky or a peculiarity of that one sample. The authors assemble six independent samples — 268 objects in all, spanning Sc I galaxies, first-ranked cluster galaxies, supernovae, Seyfert-like galaxies, Markarian galaxies and absorption-line compact galaxies — and find the asymmetry in every one of them.
Their conclusion is that the Hubble Constant is not constant across the sky at moderate distances. Overview
The document is Keilman's position paper for a debate held on 8 August 2009, headed "Debate: Einstein's Special Relativity Postulates: True or False?" It is written as a sequence of numbered slides rather than as continuous prose, and its target is not the relativists but Keilman's fellow critics of relativity. His answer to the debate question is neither "true" nor "false" but "misposed": the postulates are consequences that Einstein promoted to starting points, and arguing about their truth is arguing about the wrong thing.
Keilman's own position is unusual within the dissident literature. He accepts Special Relativity as "a classical theory and a big discovery" and defends its mathematics as "not disputable," while charging Einstein with a "phenomenal" misrepresentation in the way he presented it. What he denies is that time dilation and length contraction are physical at all — against Lorentz, who thought they were real changes caused by motion through the Aether , and against those relativists who treat them as real effects on physical systems. And he ends by reinstating an aether of his own: a four-dimensional one, absolute, and immune to the influence of matter, which is an explicit denial of general relativity.

"Special Relativity as a Subset of Autodynamics" — published at autodynamics.org under the heading AD to SR and subtitled "Special Relativity a Physically Wrong Mathematical Subset of Autodynamics" — sets out the algebraic transformation, obtained by Ricardo L Carezani in 1991, by which the special relativity expression for kinetic energy is recovered from the Autodynamics one. Carezani regarded it as among his most important results, and the timeline on the site records it as the year he "discover[ed] the mathematical conversion indicating that special relativity is a subset of Autodynamics."
Overview
The paper turns on a distinction that governs the whole of Autodynamics. Autodynamics, Carezani writes, "was derived to describe decay cases: no external energy or kinetic energy is introduced into the system. All energy comes from the particle itself" — the rocket, whose thrust is bought with its own mass. Special relativity, by contrast, describes energy "applied externally to a particle", so that the total is the rest mass plus a kinetic contribution from outside — the cannon and the cannon ball.
The transformation makes that difference into a substitution.

Write the Autodynamics kinetic energy as
E c = M [ 1 − 1 − β 2 ]
with M = m 0 c 2 for a decaying particle. For a particle receiving energy from outside, Carezani argues, the quantity in the bracket must act on the rest energy plus the kinetic energy already imparted, so M = m 0 c 2 + E c . Substituting, distributing, cancelling the common energy terms and isolating E c returns
E c = m 0 c 2 [ 1 1 − β 2 − 1 ]

Type Theory of space, time, and motion

Keywords Relativity , special relativity, simultaneity, time dilation, length contraction, Lorentz transformation, E = mc 2
Year 1905
Special relativity is the physical theory published by Albert Einstein in 1905 in the paper On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies . It describes the relationship between space and time for observers moving uniformly relative to one another, and it replaced the Galilean transformations of classical mechanics with the Lorentz transformations . In mainstream physics it is regarded as extensively confirmed by experiment.
Special relativity is also the single most-discussed subject on this wiki. It is the keyword of more papers catalogued here than any other concept in physics, and the literature indexed under it — several hundred papers, together with dozens of books — is overwhelmingly critical. The critics are not a single school. They disagree with each other about what is wrong, about what should replace the theory, and about whether anything need replace it at all. What they share is the conviction that the theory's two postulates, its derivation, its treatment of time and simultaneity, or its claimed experimental support will not survive careful examination. The speed of light in vacuum, written c , is the most heavily loaded constant in modern physics. It fixes the ratio between mass and energy, sets the scale of the electromagnetic field equations, defines the metre, and — in the form of Einstein's second postulate, that c has the same value in every inertial frame regardless of the motion of the source — supplies the foundation on which special relativity is built. Since the 1983 redefinition of the SI metre, c is no longer measured at all: it is defined as exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, and the metre is derived from it.
The literature collected on this wiki treats almost every part of that account as open. The researchers documented here do not agree with one another — some hold that c is constant but relative to a medium or a field rather than to every observer; some that the two-way speed is constant while the one-way speed is not; some that c varies with gravitational potential, with the medium, or with time; some that the constancy observed in experiments is an artefact of the instruments used to measure it; and a few that the light-speed barrier can be exceeded outright. What they share is the conviction that the second postulate was elevated to a principle before the experimental evidence could bear it, and that the 1983 redefinition has since made the question difficult even to ask, because a discrepant measurement now registers as a wrongly calibrated metre rather than as a physical result.
This article states the orthodox position, then organises the objections found in the archive by the idea at stake rather than by author.
The mainstream position
Three claims are usually run together under the heading "constancy of the speed of light", and the papers here often turn on separating them.

Abstract
The speed of light according to the Special Theory of Relativity has the same value C with respect to any inertial frame of reference in 4-dimensional pseudo-Euclidean space. An attempt to build an alternative physical model in 3-dimensional Euclidean space brings up a question: in what frame of reference does light move with the speed C? Series of experiments and mathematical reasoning suggest that: 1) the speed of a photon emitted by an atom equals to C if measured with respect to the atom if the atom is at rest or moving with a constant speed with respect to a 3-dimensional inertial frame of reference; 2) the speed of light acquires the value of a constant C near Earth, Sun and other large masses; the energy of the photon depends on the gravitational potential, 3) light has inertial properties.
Overview
Presented at the 20th Natural Philosophy Alliance conference in 2013, this paper by Nina Sotina and Nadia Lvov asks a question that special relativity dissolves rather than answers: if space is ordinary three-dimensional Euclidean space and time is independent of it, then with respect to what does light travel at c ?
Their answer is a modified emission theory. Light leaves an atom at speed c relative to that atom — Walther Ritz's ballistic hypothesis of 1908 — but does not keep that speed. As it propagates it undergoes what the authors call hidden dynamics : its velocity relaxes toward c in the frame of any large nearby mass, and does so without any loss of energy, the change in speed being compensated by a change in the photon's mass. The relativistic kinematics of Minkowski space is then, on this view, a formalism that gets the right answers by encoding a real dynamical process it does not name.

Spiritual Foundations is a 1996 book by Paramahamsa Tewari , the Indian nuclear-project engineer who developed Space Vortex Theory . It is the one book in his output that is explicitly metaphysical rather than physical, and it states the conviction that underlies all the rest: that the aakaash — the space of the Upanishads — is the single substantial reality, and that neither science nor religion can get hold of its subject until that is granted.
It is a short book, 104 pages, and it is not a treatise. It collects essays written during the years in which Tewari was building his physical theory, in a period during which, by his own account, he was also undergoing spiritual experiences. The two lines of thought are presented as one enquiry.
The argument
The book opens by refusing to take its nominal subject first. From the preface:
What is the reality of the universe? This question should be first answered before the concept of God can be analysed. Science is still in search of the basic entity that constucts the cosmos. God, therefore, will be a system too complex for science to discover. Unless the basic reality of aakaash (space) is recognized, neither science nor spirituality can have a grasp of the Creator, Sustainer and Destroyer of this gigantic phenomena that the Vedas named as Brahman.
The move being made here is the same one Tewari makes in his physics, and it is worth stating plainly because it is easy to miss. He is not arguing from scripture to a conclusion about nature. Residence Kiev, Ukraine
Known for Cold Fusion
Stanislav V. Adamenko is a Ukrainian physicist and the founder and scientific director of the Electrodynamics Laboratory "Proton-21" in Kiev, established in 1999.
Work
The laboratory's programme is the pursuit of extreme compression of matter in a small-scale terrestrial apparatus, with the aim of reaching densities approaching those of nuclear matter — conditions Adamenko describes as "stellar" and compares to the interiors of white dwarfs and neutron stars.
The method is a pulsed electron beam of up to a kilojoule, at a few hundred keV and lasting tens of nanoseconds, directed at a solid target a few tens of micrometres across. Adamenko's claim is that this acts as a "coherent driver", initiating a self-organising and self-sustaining collapse of the electron–nucleus plasma, and that the collapse produces a wholesale nuclear rearrangement of part of the target: the synthesis of elements across the whole periodic table, the creation of superheavy nuclei beyond any known element, and the conversion of radioactive nuclei into stable ones. The last of these is presented as a possible route to the treatment of nuclear waste.
The work is set out at length in Controlled Nucleosynthesis: Breakthroughs in Experiment and Theory (Springer, 2007), edited with Vladimir Vysotskii and Andrei Vysotskyy, which collects the laboratory's experimental reports and its theoretical account of the collapse. The programme has been presented mainly at the International Conference on Cold Fusion and Condensed Matter Nuclear Science meetings.
The central experimental claims — in particular the detection of stable nuclei with mass numbers between 250 and 500, and the assertion that a milligram of target material undergoes complete nuclear regeneration in each shot — have not been reproduced elsewhere.

Stanley Jeffers is an English-Canadian experimental physicist, Associate Professor (now retired) in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at York University in Toronto. He is best known in this field not for a theory of his own but for having built the principal international forum in which heterodox interpretations of quantum mechanics are argued: he was the executive local organiser of the Vigier Symposia , and co-editor of the volumes that came out of them.
His position is an unusual one among the figures documented on this wiki, and worth stating plainly. Jeffers is a conventionally credentialed experimentalist who has taken heterodox claims seriously enough to organise conferences around them, edit their proceedings, and in several cases test them in the laboratory — while frequently reporting results that do not support the claim in question. He is at once a builder of the dissenting community's institutions and one of its more exacting critics.
Education and career
Jeffers took his B.Sc. in Physics with Special Honours (A.R.C.S.) at Imperial College, University of London, in 1963, and his Ph.D. (D.I.C.) in opto-electronics at the same institution in 1968. He spent his academic career in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at York University in Toronto, where he taught undergraduate courses including The Nature and Growth of Scientific Thought .
He is a member of the International Astronomical Union and has served as an associate editor of the World Scientific Series in Contemporary Chemical Physics.

Abstract
As a Bose condensate, superconductors provide novel conditions for revisiting previously proposed couplings between electromagnetism and gravity. Strong variations in Cooper pair density, large conductivity and low magnetic permeability define superconductive and degenerate condensates without the traditional density limits imposed by the Fermi energy (??10−6 g cm 3 ). Recent experiments have reported anomalous weight loss for a test mass suspended above a rotating type II, YBCO superconductor, with the percentage change (0.05-2.1%) independent of the test mass' chemical composition and diamagnetic properties. A variation of 5 parts per 104 was reported above a stationary (non-rotating) superconductor. In experiments using a sensitive gravimeter, bulk YBCO superconductors were stably levitated in a DC magnetic field. Changes in acceleration were measured to be less than 2 parts in 108 of the normal gravitational acceleration. This result puts new limits on the strength and range of the proposed coupling between static superconductors and gravity.

Keywords perfect cosmological principle, continuous creation, Big Bang , quasi-steady state , eternal universe
Year 1948
Steady state theory is the cosmological model in which the universe has no beginning and no end, presenting on the large scale the same appearance at every epoch, with new matter created continuously to keep the mean density constant as the universe expands.
The standard account
The theory was put forward in 1948 in two papers in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society : one by Hermann Bondi and Thomas Gold , the other, on a different formal basis, by Fred Hoyle . Its governing assumption is the perfect cosmological principle — the universe is homogeneous and isotropic not only in space, as ordinary cosmology assumes, but also in time. There is therefore no privileged epoch, no "early universe," and no origin event.
The model accepted the observed expansion. To keep the perfect cosmological principle in the face of expansion, matter must appear continuously; the required rate is very small, of the order of one hydrogen atom per cubic metre every billion years, far below any rate that could be detected directly. The universe is thus infinitely old, infinitely extended, and always the same in the mean, with galaxies of every age present everywhere at every time.
The steady state model was the principal rival to the evolving hot-origin cosmology through the 1950s and early 1960s. It was Hoyle who gave the rival theory its name, using the phrase "big bang" dismissively in a 1949 BBC broadcast. The model was falsifiable in a way its rival was not: because it forbids evolution, any evidence that the distant — and therefore earlier — universe differs systematically from the nearby one counts directly against it. Abstract
The phenomenon of stellar collapse is considered from the viewpoint of the neo-Newtonian ballistic theory of light. The restrictions of the special theory of relativity are thus removed. The theory predicts that a collapsing star will expand again, and continue to alternately expand and collapse at a rate depending on the mass and greatest radius of the star. On each cycle material will be lost, including photons which appear to distant observers as the emissions of a pulsar. It is concluded that pulsars are oscillating stars, that these eventually "evaporate" away completely, and that there is no such object as a black hole.
Overview
Waldron's paper, published in Apeiron No. 7 (1990), continues an argument he began in "Do Black Holes Exist?" ( Speculations in Science and Technology , 1983). His original objection was that the gravitational energy released by a collapsing burnt-out star would blow the star apart before it reached the Schwarzschild radius. Correspondence with "a number of leading cosmologists" prompted a rethink, and this paper is the result: instead of an explosion, he now argues for an oscillation . The star collapses, turbulence and rotation halt the infall, it re-expands to nearly its original radius, and the cycle repeats, shedding matter and radiation each time. What a distant observer sees is a pulsar. There is no black hole .
The framework is what Waldron calls the "neo-Newtonian ballistic theory of light" — an emission theory in which Newton's three laws are "inviolable", Einstein's invariance postulate is rejected as "incompatible with the principle of relativity", and light consists of material particles. Overview
Stellar Metamorphosis: An Alternative for the Star Sciences is a five-page paper by Jeffrey Joseph Wolynski of Cocoa, Florida, dated 2012 and presented at the 20th Natural Philosophy Alliance Conference in July 2013.
Its thesis is a single identification: "Planet formation is star evolution… Planets are ancient stars and stars are young planets." Wolynski notes that "planet" is from αστήρ πλανήτησ, wandering star, and argues that treating the two as distinct is "the wrong root assumption", from which "there is no possible way to understand anything."
The proposed sequence is a chain of phase transitions. Quasars create matter as newborn galaxies (citing Arp and Ambartsumian); a gas cloud is ionised and compressed by a Z-pinch into a hot blue star; the plasma cools and recombines to a gas, giving first a red dwarf and then a "gas giant planet"; the gas deposits as solids and liquids, giving a rocky planet like the Earth, with the oceans condensing from its atmosphere and the Grand Canyon's layers laid down by direct deposition of gaseous silicon dioxide; and finally the dead star collides with others, producing asteroid belts and the rings and "proto-planetary disks" that are, on this reading, debris rather than nurseries.
Two further claims carry the framework. Gravitation is redefined: "This decreasing enthalpy is what gravitation is… It is not a force, is not constant… The faster the lowering of enthalpy the higher the 'gravitation'." Stephen Hawking Smoked My Socks: How Beliefs Contaminate Our Opinions — An Astrophysicist's Perspective is a 2014 book by the South African astrophysicist Hilton Ratcliffe , published by the U.S.-based Muse Harbor Publishing in November 2014.
The book asks why a handful of scientists — Stephen Hawking and Albert Einstein foremost among them — become world-famous figures, and argues that their fame has little to do with the substance of their science. Ratcliffe uses this as a starting point to examine how belief shapes and "contaminates" opinion, the tension between belief and instinct in forming a worldview, and what he characterises as the suffocating control that scientific orthodoxy exercises over dissenting ideas. It continues the sceptical, anti-consensus themes of his earlier books The Virtue of Heresy: Confessions of a Dissident Astronomer and The Static Universe: Exploding the Myth of Cosmic Expansion .

Steve Wishman is an American independent researcher based in Sacramento, California, associated with the Electric Universe model of cosmology. He is recorded among the dissident scientists catalogued in Jean de Climont's Worldwide List of Dissident Scientists ; beyond that listing and his association with the Electric Universe, little biographical detail about him is publicly documented.
Work
Wishman is associated with the Electric Universe framework, an alternative cosmology which holds that electric currents and plasma — rather than gravity alone — are the dominant organizing force in the universe. The approach draws on the laboratory plasma physics of Hannes Alfvén and was developed and popularized by figures such as Wallace Thornhill and David Talbott . It stands in contrast to the standard gravity-centered model of cosmology and is not accepted by mainstream astrophysics.

Steven B. Bryant is an American researcher and technology executive known for a mathematical critique of the derivations underlying special relativity, and for the alternative framework he calls Modern Mechanics (or Modern Classical Mechanics).
His central technical claim concerns Einstein's Spherical Wave Proof . Bryant argues that the proof establishes only that the transformed coordinates satisfy the general equation of a sphere, not that they lie on the same sphere — and that when the radii are checked, the transformed points turn out to lie on multiple spheres rather than one. Since the purpose of the proof is to establish the relationship between the constancy of the speed of light and the principle of relativity, he concludes that the relationship is not established.
His positive proposal turns on a distinction he says relativity conflates: length versus wavelength . On his account time dilation, length contraction and the twin paradox are all artefacts of using a length-based model to interpret wavelength-based observations, and he reports that equations built on the distinction fit the Michelson-Morley and Ives-Stilwell results substantially more closely than the Einstein-Lorentz equations do.
Bryant was a subject matter leader in the relativity community of the Natural Philosophy Alliance , has spoken at AAAS (American Association for the Advancement of Science) and NPA conferences at universities across the United States, and set out his framework for a general readership in Disruptive: Rewriting the Rules of Physics (2016). Steven Dinowitz is an American independent theorist, the author of Field Distortion Theory — an attempt to keep the Galilean transformations while still accounting for the experimental evidence usually taken to establish special relativity .
He is worth attention for a reason that has nothing to do with whether the theory is right. In 1991 he derived from it a specific, numerical, dated prediction about a named experiment — that CERN's Large Electron–Positron collider would prove unable to accelerate an electron past 60 GeV. The machine was built, it ran for nine years, and the prediction can be checked.
Field Distortion Theory
The theory begins with light propagation. Dinowitz proposes that the electric field surrounding a source undergoes an "aerodynamic-like distortion" when the source moves through a gravitational field . The distortion, not a change in the structure of space and time, is what produces the observed behaviour of light; the Galilean transformations are retained throughout, and the theory is offered as consistent with the existing optical evidence while suggesting new experiments.
From there he makes the move the rest depends on: a body's inertial mass is a consequence of that same field distortion . Mass therefore does not increase with velocity as such, but with velocity relative to whichever gravitational field is locally dominant in energy density — near the Earth's surface, the Earth's own field.
The full statement is " Field Distortion Theory (FDT) ", a 26-page paper in Physics Essays 9 (3) in 1996.

This article describes an ether that is not autonomous or entrained in velocity. Instead of entraining the ether a celestial body absorbs a very small amount of ether particles passing through the body. This causes a small net velocity in the average value of all particle velocities. The ether gets a small velocity in direction towards the body. This generated ether-wind follows the body like a shadow and causes gravity. Spherical symmetry means that one body is not decelerated by its own field. However, two bodies disturb the symmetry to each other and are therefore pushed in direction towards each other. The generated ether-wind cause gravity. The ether particles move with the speed c and can also transfer light. The ether particles do not collide with each other and the ether is not a gas but a special state of aggregation. Abstract
The straight line inertial path will be examined from the perspective that it is caused by pressure equilibrium in a sea of tiny aethereal whirlpools that are pressing against each other with centrifugal force while striving to dilate. This is opposite to the traditional perspective whereby centrifugal force is considered to be a consequence of the tendency of a body to move in uniform straight line motion in the absence of any Newtonian forces.
Overview
Straight Line Motion is a four-page paper by David Tombe , dated 31 May 2018 and posted to the General Science Journal . It inverts the usual order of explanation: rather than treating centrifugal force as a consequence of the tendency to move in a straight line, it treats the straight line as a consequence of centrifugal pressure in a medium.
The medium is Maxwell's, by way of Bernoulli, Tesla and Oliver Lodge, all quoted at length: "space is rendered into tiny whirlpools that are pressing against each other with centrifugal force while striving to dilate." Tombe proposes that in the absence of a radial field "the individual rotation axes of these tiny whirlpools form concentric rings around a moving object", so that the object's line of motion is at right angles to the pressure exerted on it. "When this centrifugal pressure field (inertial field) is symmetrical, the motion will constitute the straight line inertial path."
A key assertion follows: "It's a geometrical fact that a moving object has a centrifugal acceleration to every point in space that does not lie along its path of motion. This fact largely goes unnoticed, disguised in the straight line inertial path, but it manifests itself as a physical reality when the moving object is opposed by a centripetal force." A supernova is the catastrophic brightening of a star, in which a single object can for a few weeks outshine the whole galaxy that contains it. Supernovae matter far beyond stellar astrophysics because one class of them, Type Ia , is the standard candle on which the modern distance scale — and with it the claim that cosmic expansion is accelerating — rests.
The standard account
Supernovae are sorted spectroscopically. Core-collapse events (Types II, Ib and Ic) are held to occur when a massive star exhausts its nuclear fuel, its iron core collapses, and the infalling envelope rebounds; most of the released energy escapes as neutrinos. Type Ia events show no hydrogen and are attributed instead to the thermonuclear detonation of a white dwarf that has been driven toward the Chandrasekhar mass of about 1.4 solar masses by accretion from, or merger with, a companion.
The nearest supernova of the modern era, SN 1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud, was seen on 23 February 1987 and remains the only one for which a neutrino burst was detected. Its expanding, strikingly symmetric triple-ring structure has been imaged for decades.
Type Ia events are treated as standardisable candles: their peak brightness correlates with the decline rate of the light curve, so the shape of the curve is used to correct the peak and yield a distance. In 1998 two teams reported that distant Type Ia supernovae appeared fainter than a freely coasting universe predicts, and this was interpreted as accelerating expansion driven by dark energy . A second argument drawn from the same data is that supernova light curves at redshift z appear stretched by a factor of 1+ z , which is presented as a direct observation of cosmological time dilation .

It is an applied test of Suntola's Dynamic Universe (DU) model against the Type Ia supernova data that underwrote the discovery of accelerating cosmic expansion.
Its claim is narrow and quantitative rather than programmatic: that a one-parameter magnitude–redshift relation derived from a zero-energy balance in a spherically closed, expanding four-dimensional space fits the Riess et al. 2004 supernova compilation at least as well as the two-parameter standard cosmology relation, and does so without dark energy , without accelerating expansion, and without any assumption about Ω m , Ω Λ or the Hubble constant.
Abstract
Recent observations on the redshift and magnitude of distant supernovae have raised fundamental questions of the cosmological structure and the development of space. Interpretation of the observations with the standard cosmology model suggests accelerating expansion of space which requires an assumption of unknown dark energy working against gravitation at cosmological distances. This paper presents an analysis which shows that the observed magnitude redshift relationship is in an excellent agreement with the prediction derived by assuming a zero energy balance of motion and gravitation in an expanding 4-sphere. Such an approach can be regarded as Einstein-deSitter expansion in the fourth dimension, suggesting a decelerating expansion velocity until zero in infinity.

Abstract
HHigh redshift broadening of supernovae light curves, taken at face value, is the only direct evidence for expansion and is often used to discount Tired Light Theories. However, the authors of these papers look at high redshifts since these results are said to give "conclusive evidence for expansion." But what of the smaller redshifts?, what do they show? This paper reviews supernovae aging data and shows that if we ignore Malmquist biases and that fact that brighter supernova Ia do have intrinsically broader light curves, then the main stream supernovae evidence is that whilst there may be expansion at high redshifts, there is no time dilation and therefore no expansion at low redshifts. That is, if we are to believe the main stream version of supernovae light curves then we must believe that the Universe is presently static. These results are then compared to average Hydrogen cloud separation in the Lyman alpha forest in quasar spectra. These also show that at high redshifts the average spacing between Hydrogen clouds reduces as the redshift increases ? showing evidence that the clouds are moving further apart with time and therefore expansion. However, at low redshifts the average spacing is constant - again showing a static Universe in the region. Is it just coincidence that both sets of data show expansion at high redshifts and a static Universe at low redshifts?
Together, both sets of data are consistent with a Universe that did expand in the past but stopped expanding some time ago. The density of the Universe would then be equal to the critical density and we would have reached the point where the expansion has been arrested. Surrounding, an alternative theory to dark matter, is presented. It is a modification of Newton's law. Survey of Critical Thinkers Today was a live session presented by David de Hilster on 24 October 2020 in the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society live session series.
David de Hilster, host of Dissident Science will talk about who are the movers and shakers outside mainstream science. Who is in and who is out? What are the latest models critical thinkers are working on? Chat live with David and other critical thinkers live on YouTube and Facebook.
Summary
David de Hilster speaking himself, on what he called a shocking fact: that long-standing members of the society are not familiar with most of the areas its own people work in. His case in point was expansion tectonics, which claims the earth is gaining mass at a subatomic level — a claim with large implications for physics — and which he had found several regular participants had simply never thought about. Since most of the work is interdisciplinary, he argued, isolation is bad for one's own work: somebody else may be doing the thing that changes the field.
He also answered two standing charges. That dissidents have no consensus — he promised a chart at the end showing considerable agreement among the newer models. And that they throw everything away — on the contrary, a new model must account for everything the standard model accounts for, which he said is not a high bar given that the standard model supplies no physicality for light, magnetism, electric fields or current.
Who dissidents are
People who can look for truth without financial or peer pressure — often the retired, often without a degree in the area of interest. He pressed the question of what expertise now means when the same reading is available to anyone, and noted that dissidents are heterogeneous by nature: no single model, disagreement over charge, over the ether.

"Systems in Relative Motion" is a paper by Ricardo L Carezani defending the Autodynamics velocity-sum equation against the objection that it gives visibly wrong answers at everyday speeds. It is written as a running exchange with a physicist who raised that objection, and it is the fullest statement of Carezani's distinction between kinematics and dynamics.
Overview
The Autodynamics velocity sum is
β s u m = 1 − ( 1 − β 1 2 ) ( 1 − β 2 2 ) …
Carezani's correspondent points out that for two velocities of 1 km/h this returns 1.41 km/h rather than 2 km/h, and concludes that Autodynamics is therefore wrong. Carezani concedes the arithmetic without reservation — "You are right. There is no mistake in your calculation" — and answers that the two calculations are about different things.
The argument
Kinematics against dynamics
The distinction Carezani draws is between composing velocities without expending energy (kinematics) and composing them by expending it (dynamics). Classical mechanics gives 2 km/h and special relativity 1.9999 km/h because both are answering a kinematic question; Autodynamics gives 1.41 km/h because it is answering a dynamic one, in which the second increment of velocity has to be paid for out of the moving body's own mass.

Abstract
The second of two papers arguing that the theory of moving charge carriers cannot explain the electrical conduction of the Hall effect . Part II attacks the concept of the positively charged "hole" as a category mistake, and proposes instead that the sign of the Hall coefficient is governed by crystal structure , within a model in which conduction is the propagation of a state of charge distribution rather than a flow of charges.
The argument against holes
Marinsek's target is the standard account in which conduction in a solid is carried by electrons and by holes — vacancies in a filled band treated as particles of effective positive charge. His objection is not quantitative but conceptual, and he states it as a category mistake : "a successive occurrence of different holes is not identical with the movement of one hole." A hole, on his account, is simply the previous location of an electron; a location cannot move unless the atom moves, which the theory does not claim.
He works this through the "row of seats" analogy used in textbook expositions and in the Wikipedia article on the electron hole, in which people shift one seat along and the empty seat appears to travel the other way. The analogy fails, he argues, on the same point: seat #4 does not move towards the edge of the row, and all that occurs is a succession of empty seats.
From this he draws the stronger claim, which is where the ontological objection lies. Treating the absence of an electron as a particle amounts to a transubstantiation of an empty place into a positron — a creation ex nihilo . Tadayoshi Ohmori is a Japanese electrochemist known for his experimental research on Cold Fusion and low-energy nuclear transmutation. Working at Hokkaido University in Sapporo, he collaborated with Tadahiko Mizuno on electrolysis experiments that reported excess heat and the anomalous production of new elements.
Education
B.S. in chemistry — Hokkaido University, 1962
Doctorate in electrochemistry — Hokkaido University, 1988
Biography
He served as a research associate at the Catalysis Research Center of Hokkaido University, where he carried out much of his work on electrochemical anomalies.
Scientific contributions
Ohmori's research centered on electrolysis experiments in which unexpected heat and elemental changes were reported at electrode surfaces. In studies of light water electrolysis using gold electrodes, he and his collaborators reported the appearance of iron atoms together with the generation of excess energy. Further experiments described the formation of mercury, krypton, nickel and iron with anomalous isotopic compositions on or in gold electrodes, and silicon and magnesium with anomalous isotopic compositions in precipitates separated from gold electrodes electrolyzed at very high current densities. These observations were interpreted by Ohmori and his co-workers as evidence of nuclear transmutation.
Together with Tadahiko Mizuno , Ohmori also investigated plasma electrolysis, in which a plasma is formed at an electrode surface during high-voltage electrolysis. Using real-time heat calibration, they reported that the measured heat output could substantially exceed the input electrical power. This body of work is frequently cited within the cold fusion and low-energy nuclear reaction research literature.

Taichi Higashiyama is a Japanese nuclear engineer who, as a graduate student in the Department of Nuclear Engineering at Osaka University, was lead author of a 2003 attempt to replicate the transmutation results reported by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.
Working with Hiroyuki Miyamaru and Akito Takahashi at Osaka and with Mitsuru Sakano of MHI, he carried out three runs of deuterium gas permeation through layered palladium samples supplied by MHI, with caesium deposited on the surface, and reported nanogram quantities of praseodymium afterwards. The results were presented as Replication Of MHI Transmutation Experiment By D2 Gas Permeation Through Pd Complex at the 10th International Conference on Cold Fusion (ICCF10) in Cambridge, Massachusetts in August 2003, and interpreted in terms of Takahashi's multi-body deuteron fusion model.
The paper is unusually candid about the experimental difficulties encountered, reporting a faulty vacuum gauge, suspected moisture ingress, a gas shortage and lost data among its three runs, and describing the work as a first report.

search_text:
Title The 1855 Weber-Kohlrausch Experiment (The Speed of Light)
Read in full Link to paper
Author(s) David Tombe
Published 2019
Journal General Science Journal
Abstract
In the year 1855, German physicists Wilhelm Eduard Weber and Rudolf Kohlrausch performed an experiment with a Leyden jar and established the ratio between electrostatic and electrodynamic units of charge. This ratio became known as Weber’s constant and it is numerically equal to c√2, where c is the speed of light. In 1857, another German physicist Gustav Robert Kirchhoff used Weber’s constant to conclude that electric signals travel along a wire at the speed of light. A few years later in 1861, Scottish physicist James Clerk Maxwell was working on the physical medium responsible for magnetic lines of force and he had established a linkage between its transverse elasticity and the ratio of electrostatic to electromagnetic units of charge. Electromagnetic units of charge are related to electrodynamic units by a factor of √2. In order to evaluate this ratio, Maxwell looked up Weber’s results, and on converting Weber’s constant into electromagnetic units, the speed of light was exposed. This paper sets out to establish the fundamental origins of the speed of light.
Overview
Dated 14 April 2019 and posted to the General Science Journal , this paper by David Tombe of Northern Ireland is a historical reconstruction with a thesis attached. Its subject is the experiment Wilhelm Weber and Rudolf Kohlrausch performed in 1855, which measured the ratio between the electrostatic and electrodynamic units of charge and so, unexpectedly, produced a velocity.
Tombe traces what followed: Kirchhoff's use of that ratio in 1857 to conclude that electric signals travel along a wire at the speed of light; and Maxwell's use of it in 1861, while working on the elastic medium responsible for magnetic lines of force, to expose the speed of light directly and connect it to the transverse elasticity of the luminiferous medium.

From the beginning of time, man has been awed by the sight of the night sky. Ever since, we have tried to probe its depths, fathom it secrets, and find our position among the stars. Comets zoom through the void past us (some even hits us.)
With amazement, the structure of the milky Way is defined, including us on Earth as part of this Milky Way Galaxy. The scope of our Universe grows, finding ourselves and our local family of twenty or so galaxies sailing along among billions of galaxies. There's more, the apparent staid motion of the night sky unveils itself to expose a massive outrushing in all directions; that points to a violent beginning and an undefined ending.
More mysteries are found. Quasars, the very faint, shining star-like pinpoints of light are found near the edges of our Universe. The mystery of Quasars staggers the imagination, expanding unbelievable amounts of energy, greater than any galaxy times a hundred or more.

Abstract
In D. P. Sheehan (ed.), Frontiers of Time (Melville, NY: AIP Conference Proceedings ), pp. 75-88. A new event is defined as an intervention in the time reversible dynamical trajectories of particles in a system. New events are then assumed to be quantum fluctuations in the spatial and momentum coordinates, and mental action is assumed to work by ordering such fluctuations. It is shown that when the cumulative values of such fluctuations in a mean free path of a molecule are magnified by molecular interaction at the end of that path, the momentum of a molecule can be changed from its original direction to any other direction. In this way mental action can produce effects through the ordering of thermal motions. Examples are given which show that the ordering of 10 4 -10 5 molecules is sufficient to (a) produce detectible PK results and (b) open sufficient ion channels in the brain to initiate a physical action. The relationship of the above model to the arrow of time is discussed.
Overview
Jean E. Burns's contribution to the Frontiers of Time conference is an attempt to give a quantitative, physically constrained account of how mental action could affect matter — and to tie that account to the origin of the arrow of time. Its organising idea is the new event : an intervention in the time-reversible dynamical trajectories of particles, something "not predicted by those laws". Because the dynamical laws of physics run equally well in either time direction, Burns argues, once a trajectory is fixed by initial conditions it admits no later alteration; the only way a new event can enter is by changing the initial conditions themselves. Random quantum events, free will and psychokinesis (PK) are all treated as instances of the same formal category.

The Dynamic Theory "adopts generalizations of the classical laws of thermodynamics as the basis for a new view of all physical phenomena." Williams concedes this "may at first seem preposterous", since mechanical systems obey laws of motion while the thermodynamic laws have never yielded equivalent equations for thermodynamic systems. But he argues the implication runs the other way: if equations of motion can be obtained from generalized thermodynamic laws, then "the irreversibility so prominent in thermodynamics would also be embodied within these equations." Abstract
An asymptote is a goal that can probably never be reached, and if reached, cannot be crossed. If crossed, there may be no return. There are at least six asymptotes that apply to our universe. A box has six sides. Consequently, we can use the metaphor that our universe is an asymptotic box. The six asymptotes of the natural world that apply to our universe are birth, death, the speed of light, absolute zero, gravitational collapse limit, and the superforce. There is also an asymptotic box of scientific reasoning. The paper will define the asymptotes and then discuss various consequences.
Overview
Robert Heaston's essay is a philosophical argument rather than a calculation — he says explicitly that "no mathematics or equations will be used." Its occasion was the May 2003 Scientific American cover feature announcing that parallel universes "probably real... should exist in four different ways," and his purpose is to argue the opposite case: that our universe is bounded by asymptotes we cannot pass, and that theories which cross them have left physics behind.
He identifies six such bounds and arranges them as the faces of a box. Birth and death form the front and back; the speed of light and the gravitational collapse limit form the two sides; absolute zero is the floor and what he calls the superforce is the ceiling. The pairing is deliberate: birth and death are limits on time, light speed and collapse are limits on space, absolute zero and the superforce are limits on matter, so that the box's structure follows from the three basic units.

The Atom is a 1920 book by Albert Cushing Crehore setting out an alternative to the Bohr model of the atom. It is not an exposition of accepted atomic physics but an argument against the theory that had just become standard, together with a rival theory of Crehore's own — one in which the hydrogen atom has two electrons rather than one, a whole series of spectral lines is emitted in a single operation rather than one line per jump, and gravitation is derived from the motion of the electrons inside atoms .
The book is the mathematical statement of a programme Crehore had described without equations three years earlier in The Mystery of Matter and Energy: Recent Progress as to the Structure of Matter (1917), and it was followed the same year by The New Physics .
Why the book was written
Crehore explains in the first pages that he would ordinarily have published this work as a series of papers in the technical journals, as he had done for many years, but that the argument needed more space than a journal would give and that condensing it would weaken rather than strengthen it. He is explicit about what he is doing:
It would be false modesty to try to disguise the fact that the subject of atomic theory is treated in a new form from the beginning to the end of the volume… This has made it necessary to emphasize the points where the current theory of the atom, that due to Dr. N. Bohr, is deficient.
He adds that Bohr's work is "most suggestive, and as marking an epoch in the progress of atomic theory." The dispute is with the theory, not with its author.

Abstract
The elementary building unit of the Universe - quantum connection of opposite poles (quantum dipole) represents the elementary quantum of space. The Universe pulsates thanks to its dialectic contradiction between attraction and repulsion. The cosmic expansion is caused by systematic expelling of new quantum dipoles accompanied with the transition of the Universe from one quantum state to the next by elementary quantum jump, which represents the elementary quantum of time. This fact can be expressed by simple space-time equation of the Universe, which has important consequences and enables to calculate such cosmic characteristics like mass and energy of the Universe, its volume, average density, radius of cosmic curvature and others.
Overview
Peter Kohut builds a cosmology from a single combinatorial postulate. The universe consists of poles, positive and negative, and every positive pole is connected to every negative one; each connection is a "quantum dipole" and constitutes an elementary quantum of space. Expansion proceeds by expelling new pole pairs, and each such expulsion is an elementary quantum of time.
The arithmetic follows immediately. In symmetric state k there are k positive and k negative poles, hence k ² connections, so the volume goes as the square of the elapsed time:
V k = k ², and in dimensional form V = zt ².
This is what Kohut calls the basic quantum space-time equation of the universe, and the rest of the paper works out its consequences: the Hubble parameter, the age, the relation between the speed of light and the rate of cosmic expansion, the total mass and energy, and the radius of curvature of a universe treated as the three-dimensional surface of a four-dimensional sphere.

Abstract
The problem addressed by the present work refers to a sequence of ideas, which have been worked out recently by Lenard, namely, whether it might be possible to demonstrate an absolute reference system, the primordial ether, using Michelson's interference experiment (M.I.). The negative outcome of Michelson's experiment in the usual setting, namely, with terrestrial light, has shown, according to Lenard's interpretation, that the ether carrying terrestrial light waves should be considered as taking part in the movement of the earth. This, however, needs not be the case with extraterrestrial light as Lenard has shown. It could be that light quanta from extraterrestrial sources running with the primordial ether were still linked on the earth to the primordial ether, which should lead to an at least partially positive outcome of the M.I. with extraterrestrial light. A negative outcome should permit elucidating the behaviour of light quanta entering the ether of different property. In the following I will report on experiments conducted with extraterrestrial light.
Originally published as " Über das Verhalten des Lichtes außerirdischer Lichtquellen ," Annalen der Physik , V73, pp. 105-126 (1924).

It is a real interferometer campaign, carried out at the Königstuhl observatory above Heidelberg between March and July 1923 and submitted on 30 July 1923, and it belongs to the small class of Michelson-type experiments performed with starlight rather than a laboratory lamp.

The Big Bang Exploded is essential reading for all cosmologists and their students because existing textbooks on Cosmology and Astrophysics contain numerous errors in Thermodynamics and this book aims to correct these mistakes. It will also be of considerable value to students and lecturers in all science and technology, conveying "a feel for Thermodynamics".
The Hot Big Bang Theory postulates that the early Universe was at a very high temperature, and that the expansion of the Universe automatically brought about cooling from high to low temperatures. But the belief by cosmologists that expanding gases always cool down is not true; the free expansion of an ideal gas is a constant temperature process.
The nub of this subject is that thermodynamic calculations on the Hot Big Bang Theory, when done correctly, show conclusively that the theory is fallacious (PART 3). But first it is necessary to show both the basis for doing the calculations and the physical data required. Therefore PART 1 provides the groundwork for thermodynamic calculations and PART 2 analyzes the errors in books on Cosmology.
The book includes extensive thermodynamic calculations for hydrogen and a Temperature-Entropy Diagram. - Excerpted from the Introduction

Plasma physicist Lerner opens one of science's inner rooms to a popular audience in this headline-making history of time, space and the humanistic sociology of science. Illustrated.

From Library Journal
From Steven Weinberg's The First Three Minutes (Basic, 1976. o.p.; 1988. pap.) to Stephen Hawking's A Brief History of Time ( LJ 4/15/88), numerous science popularizations have expounded the Big Bang Theory for the origin of the universe as indisputable fact. Readers of those books will find this one startling and intriguing. Lerner, a plasma physicist, points out flaws in the Big Bang model and proposes an alternative theory: an eternal, self-sustaining "plasma" universe where electromagnetic fields within conducting gases provide other, simpler explanations for observed phenomena. His contention that the Big Bang is merely a repackaged creation myth is presumptuous, but well argued. To present a current scientific controversy to a general audience risks, on one hand, misleading the public and, on the other, circumventing the peer review process. This book, however, makes valid points in a convincing manner and does neither. Recommended for general science collections.
- Gregg Sapp, Montana State Univ. Libs., Bozeman

Abstract
When atomic explosions occur above a city, explosive radiations move outward, and away, and also move inward and toward the earth's center. It was the inward force that destroyed two cities in Japan. For convenience we can label the inward pointing reactions as "implosive" when directed "downward" toward the center of a spherical mass like the earth or sun. In all events, the actions and reactions must follow Sir Isaac Newton's third law: "For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction." There is nothing strange about this old truth, but too often we forget or neglect to account for both.

Its argument proceeds in four steps before reaching black holes at all.
Carroll accepts time dilation as an experimental fact: "the period of the frequency is increased by the act of putting the clock into motion", f = f 0 √(1−v²/c²). Abstract
The paper carries no separate abstract. Its opening statement of purpose, in the author's own words, reads:
It is often claimed that cosmology became a true scientific inquiry with the advent of the General Theory of Relativity. A few subsequent putative observations have been misconstrued in such a way as to support the prevailing Big Bang model by which the Universe is alleged to have burst into existence from an infinitely dense point-mass singularity. Yet it can be shown that the General Theory of Relativity and the Big Bang model are in conflict with well-established experimental facts.
Black holes are not without cosmological significance in view of the many claims routinely made for them, and so they are treated here in some detail. But the theory of black holes is riddled with contradictions and has no valid basis in observation. Nobody has ever found a black hole, even though claims for their discovery are now made on an almost daily basis. Nobody has ever found an infinitely dense point-mass singularity and nobody has ever found an event horizon, the tell-tale signatures of the black hole, and so nobody has ever found a black hole. In actuality, astrophysical scientists merely claim that there are phenomena observed about a region that they cannot see and so they illogically conclude that the unseen region must be a black hole, simply because they believe in black holes. In this way they can and do claim the presence of a black hole as they please. But that is not how science is properly done.

"The Catt Question Background" is an article by Harry Hamlin Ricker published on 5 June 2021 on Beyond Mainstream . Ricker argues that the difficulty most readers have with the Catt Question is not a difficulty with the question itself but with the word electricity , which he holds has never been given a clear and consistent definition in physical science.
He traces the confusion to the term being used for two quite different concepts — a property of fundamental particles on one hand, and something else again in the treatment that follows Oersted's discovery — and contends that no meaningful discussion of the Catt Question is possible until that ambiguity is resolved.

The Cosmic Microwave Background CMB was a live session presented by Harry Hamlin Ricker on 5 October 2024 in the John Chappell Natural Philosophy Society live session series.
The CMB will be discussed from its discovery, and interpretation, to modern satellite measurements including COBE, WMAP, and Plank.
Summary
Having given a session on Lambda-CDM cosmology, Harry Ricker found he could not answer a simple question — what exactly is the cosmic microwave background? — and set out to trace it from the theory to the satellites. His conclusion is about the story rather than the physics: the standard account is constructed by hindsight, and the details do not fit it. The session began half an hour late after StreamYard problems forced him to restart his computer.
Who actually predicted it
The textbooks say Gamow predicted the background and that Penzias and Wilson confirmed it by accident. Ricker went to the sources and found otherwise. Gamow's 1946 paper contains nothing about microwave background radiation; it postulates neutrons decaying into protons and electrons in a hot early state. Alpher and Herman's 1948 paper, which corrects Gamow, gives about 5 K — but for the remnant gas , not for any radiation.
The prediction Ricker credits comes from the Princeton group. Dicke's own account has the hot cosmology in disfavour — probably, Ricker thought, because it could not synthesise the heavier elements — and revived by Hoyle and Tayler's work on helium around 1962. What the Princeton group added, and what is now forgotten, is that their motivation was an oscillating universe: a closed universe contracting to a hot bounce and re-expanding, which avoids having to assume the energy of the universe at t = 0. On an immense scale these holes are uniformly spread through an endless space; on the scale of the visible universe they are not, because they were already concentrated by gravity while embedded in earlier universes. Abstract
The idea of the (perfect) cosmological principle (CP), viz. that the Universe presents the same aspect from any place at any time, is traced to the ancient Greek philosophers, who also suggested how such a cosmic order might work. The antithesis of this view, i.e. the Aristotelian-Ptolemaic world-picture, was to become the hallmark of the Dark Ages. The Copernican revolution constitutes the first step by science in a modern direction, and the advance of science is thus seen as a succession of world pictures, all entred on local systems, in a hierarchical progression. We demonstrate that the prevailing picture of the Universe as an evolving system is still trapped in a local mode of thinking: the Copernican revolution is unfinished.
Overview
Toivo Jaakkola of the University of Helsinki opens the fourth issue of Apeiron (February 1989) with a wide-ranging review arguing that cosmology has never properly adopted its own founding principle. His subject is the perfect cosmological principle — that the Universe "presents the same aspect from any place at any time" — which he takes to be the only genuinely cosmological standpoint, the prefix "perfect" having in his view "only historical value". The restricted principle of the standard model, which imposes uniformity in space but permits evolution in time, is for Jaakkola a half-measure: it treats the Universe as one more evolving system among systems, and so remains "trapped in a local mode of thinking". His central historical claim is that the Copernican revolution — the successive dethronement of Earth, Sun and Galaxy from the centre — is unfinished, because the modern picture still places us at a privileged moment even if not at a privileged place.

Abstract
The dependence of the frequency shift of photons on the cosine of the angle made with a gravitational field is an approximation because of the fact that the photon's trajectory changes such as to bring the photon closer to the mass as it passes. Therefore it dives up out of a slightly deeper well than it dived down into upon passing a mass. Therefore the red shift leaving will be slightly greater than the blue shift approaching. It follows that photons should have a slight residual red shift upon passing those masses in space that are either stationary, moving parallel to, or moving toward the trajectory. This shift is proposed as the main cause of the cosmological red shift since masses moving away from the trajectory should be a minority.

Abstract
A new atomic model is described which builds atoms out of alternating protons and electrons. Unlike the currently accepted planetary atomic model developed by Bohr and Rutherford, the nucleus is not a compact sphere of protons and neutrons which are surrounded by a cloud of electrons. Rather, the atoms are built up like Lego bricks into octahedral shapes. These shapes give rise to locations on the atoms for other atoms to dock and form molecules. These shapes also explain many of the observed properties of the atoms such as the observed ionization energies, spectra, fission fragments and the allowed isotopes for an atom. This model eliminates the need for the strong force and significantly simplifies our understanding of how atoms are constructed using only the electrostatic force.
Overview
The Cubic Atomic Model is a five-page paper by Franklin Hu , presented at the 20th Natural Philosophy Alliance Conference in July 2013. It proposes replacing the Bohr–Rutherford picture with a space-filling lattice: atoms are built from alternating protons and electrons stacked like Lego bricks, with no compact nucleus, no orbiting electrons, and no strong force.
The construction begins with a single proton and a single electron in contact, held together by Coulomb attraction and prevented from merging by having finite radii. Helium adds a second proton and electron in a checkerboard arrangement, plus two neutrons — which Hu takes to be proton–electron pairs — giving a cube. Heavier atoms are built by adding deuterium layers, first along an axis and then to the sides to keep the structure compact, so that large atoms take an octahedral or cross shape. Hu notes that gold crystallises in octahedra and reads this as evidence that the gold atom is itself octahedral.

Abstract
Voltage is shown to be a mathematical confection much like electric current and charge were. None of the above entities have ever been measured regardless of the names of the instruments.
Overview
Written in December 2011 and posted to the General Science Journal , this five-page paper by Forrest Bishop extends a demolition begun by others. Oliver Heaviside and Ivor Catt , he writes, "already offered up electric charge and its electric current"; now voltage must follow them onto the shelf "next to the museum exhibits marked Caloric and Phlogiston". The abstract states the thesis plainly: "Voltage is shown to be a mathematical confection much like electric current and charge were. None of the above entities have ever been measured regardless of the names of the instruments."
What can be measured
Bishop begins epistemologically. Length, angle, time, force and energy are taken as directly measurable; mass is not, since a balance measures a gravitational force and an accelerometer a resistance to acceleration, with mass "mathematically inferred from the measurement of the forces or energies: it is one further step away from direct knowledge."
Impedance in place of charge
The fundamental entity, on the Catt account Bishop adopts, is the transverse electromagnetic wave — "a shock-wave slab of Energy Current", a half-cycle square wave of vanishing thickness, propagating at c through the wave impedance Z 0 ≈ 376.73 Ω. He proposes the pair { c , Z 0 } as more fundamental than the permittivity and permeability, on the ground that "there is no way to measure the square root of a fundamental physical property or process: if there were, the unit would not be fundamental", and asks "what does the square root of length mean physically?"

Abstract
Astronomers use the Doppler-shifted absorption (dark) lines in the spectra of moving astronomic bodies to measure their radial velocities respect to Earth. A dark line, however, is the absence of radiation. How, then, can it be red-shifted or blue-shifted in any sense? This paper investigates this problem trying to comply with QM, and with both, the classical Doppler effect and its relativistic version. For relativity this is the problem: the Doppler-shifted dark lines are produced by absorption in the atmosphere of the selfsame star that emits the radiation. So it looks like a Doppler shift without relative motion. For QM the problem is how to harmonize the frequency shift with Planck's quantum relation, E=hf , where the frequency f is uniquely defined by a given energy level of a given atom in a stationary frame of reference. How can it be Doppler-shifted, by the macroscopic motion of the atom? Between 1918 and 1932, Bohr, Schroedinger, Dirac, and Fermi studied a similar problem, developing a quantum theory of the Doppler effect. They criticized and improved what each other said. Yet, in this paper preference will be given to the complete classical version of the Doppler formula, explained as a double Doppler effect with time difference between emission and reception. A "bonus" prediction of the paper is a non-relativistic diffraction experiment in which the cosmic motion of the Earth might be detected.

Abstract
Summary: It is shown directly from the Maxwell equations that the velocity of an electron with average v will oscillate about that value, giving rise to a non-radiating electromagnetic wave in the neighborhood of the electron. The oscillations are characterized by the de Broglie relation, which is normally simply postulated. Applying the result, the wave-particle paradox of electron diffraction by a double slit is resolved: the electron goes through only one aperture, but the wave surrounding it is diffracted by both of them. In the neighborhood of the electron the group velocity of the diffracted field is slowed to that of the electron, giving rise to the observed diffraction pattern.

The Dynamic Theory - A New View of Space-Time-Matter (2011) is the full technical statement of the theory Pharis E Williams developed over some thirty years. At 467 pages it supplies the derivations behind conclusions he had published piecemeal since 1981.
The book's full subtitle states its programme outright: the thermodynamic foundations of a five dimensional universe requiring currently known physical theories as subsets is presented along with new physics .
Its governing ambition is unusually austere. Williams starts from the three laws of classical thermodynamics — nothing else — and argues that Newtonian mechanics, relativity and quantum mechanics all follow from them, together with a series of predictions the standard theories do not make.

Entropy and a limiting velocity
The first move joins the First and Second Laws to produce entropy for mechanical as well as thermodynamic systems. Williams reads entropy physically, as "energy that becomes unavailable", and finds that it becomes infinite as velocity approaches a universal limiting velocity .

The limiting velocity in turn introduces velocity-dependent forces that vanish as that velocity is approached.
Systems of constant entropy are then the most stable that can occur in nature — and systems whose mechanical entropy stays constant are shown, on Williams's derivation, to obey quantum mechanical equations .

This history of the universe is based on the single assumption that the mass of the electron gradually decreases over time. Near the beginning of the universe, the proton and the electron had identical masses and were a Primordial Matter/ Antimatter Pair. After a chain annihilation of about 256 cycles, the electron's mass had decreased to the point where it could no longer annihilate with the proton. This left the 2256 electrons and protons that we have in the universe today. At this stage, protons and electrons could combine to form neutrons but not atoms. Long after, at the point where the electron became small enough to couple with a proton into a hydrogen atom, the neutrons began to decay and hydrogen atoms began to emit large quantities of photons. This initial burst of photons had the same wavelengths as the 2.7˚ Cosmic Blackbody Radiation spectrum of today. Since this very cold time, the temperature for hydrogen radiation has increased from 2.7˚ K to about 3000˚ K. The rate of the electron's gradual mass decrease can be determined by measuring the Hubble Constant. In the past, when the electron had more mass, the atomic spectra from distant galaxies had longer wavelengths and thus appears red shifted to us today. As the electron loses mass, and the atomic spectra heats up, the volume of atoms decreases. Heavy elements at the earth's center lose volume more slowly than the light elements in the earth's crust. It is this effect that drives plate tectonics and causes the continents to separate.

The Expanding Earth: Some Consequences of Dirac's Gravitation Hypothesis is a 1971 book by the physicist Pascual Jordan , published by Pergamon Press. It is an English translation (by Arthur Beer) of his 1966 German work Die Expansion der Erde (Braunschweig: Friedrich Vieweg).
Overview
Jordan takes up Paul Dirac's "large numbers" hypothesis of a gradual weakening of the gravitational constant G over cosmic time, and works out its geophysical consequences. He argues that, as gravity has weakened, the Earth has slowly expanded — swelling from an initial ball perhaps only about 7,000 km in diameter to its present size — and he connects this to continental drift, the growth of the ocean basins, and other geological evidence. The book is a rare instance of a major theoretical physicist developing the Expanding-Earth idea from a specific cosmological hypothesis.
About the author
Pascual Jordan (1902–1980) was a German theoretical physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics and quantum field theory (the Born–Heisenberg–Jordan "three-man paper," and Jordan–Wigner quantization). In his later career he worked on cosmology and gravitation, including scalar-tensor ("Jordan–Brans–Dicke") theories of varying gravity, of which the Expanding Earth was a proposed consequence.

Its subject, as the title states, is the distinction on which Marinov's entire programme rests. Every classic determination of the speed of light — and the Michelson–Morley experiment with it — measures a two-way value, sending light out and back over a closed path, so that any anisotropy in the outward leg is cancelled by the return. The Farce of Physics is a book by Bryan G Wallace (1933–1997), copyright 1993, arguing that "modern theoretical physics has become to a large degree, little more than an elaborate farce." It is part memoir, part polemic and part sociology of science: an account of Wallace's roughly fifty-year career as a physicist working outside the academic mainstream, organised around his contention that Einstein's second postulate — the constancy of the velocity of light — is contradicted by interplanetary radar data and is the load-bearing assumption of everything built on it.
It was never issued by a publisher. Wallace circulated it over the early internet, and it remains freely readable in full; see Reading the book below.
The central argument
Wallace states the thesis of the book most compactly in Chapter 4, prompted by a reader's question in Marilyn vos Savant's newspaper column about what single discovery would overturn modern science:
Einstein's special relativity theory with his second postulate that the speed of light in space is constant is the linchpin that holds the whole range of modern physics theories together. Shatter this postulate, and modern physics becomes an elaborate farce!
His evidence for shattering it is the one he had pressed since 1969: that published interplanetary radar data, in particular the 1961 radar contact with Venus, fit a classical c + v relative velocity better than a constant c . The book's wider claim is that the physics community's failure to engage with this is not an accident but a symptom — of funding structures, of peer review, and of what he regards as physics having taken on the character of a faith.
The title is a deliberate echo of Fritjof Capra's The Tao of Physics , which Wallace quotes

A discussion of the fundamental nature of the physical constant alpha that quantifies the strength of the electromagnetic interaction between elementary charged particles. Hosted by Ian Cowan.
Summary
James Arathoon began by disclaiming expertise. What prompted the talk was exasperation: the popular treatments of the fine-structure constant oscillate between presenting it as an unexplainable mystery and offering numerology, and he wanted to do some calculations instead — even wrong ones — to see where they lead.
Why it matters
α = e 2 /4πε 0 ℏ c is the only dimensionless number that can be made from these constants of nature, all units cancelling. Its inverse is close to but not exactly 137.
Arathoon stressed something usually left out: the constant now sits at the heart of the SI system. Where once only the speed of light was fixed by definition, the Planck constant and the elementary charge are fixed too, so the metre follows from c , the kilogram from h and the ampere from e — and a measurement of α ties the system together. The permeability of free space, formerly defined as exactly 4π × 10 −7 , is now a measured quantity that happens to sit within the error bounds of that value.
The open questions he set out: whether α approximates a notional irrational number as π does; whether it can be computed by an algorithm independent of experiment; and whether it is constant through the history of the universe.

Abstract
In the year 1855, German physicists Wilhelm Eduard Weber and Rudolf Kohlrausch performed a landmark experiment of profound significance. By discharging a Leyden jar (a capacitor), they linked the speed of light to the ratio between electrostatic and electrodynamic units of charge.
This experiment was electromagnetism’s Rosetta Stone because the result can be used to, (i) identify the speed of light as the speed of circulation of electric current, (ii) identify the speed of light as the speed of electromagnetic waves through a dielectric solid that pervades all of space, while noting that inertial centrifugal force and dipole fields share in common an inverse cube law in distance.
